Title: Repository, CI skeleton and definition of done
User story: Set up content repo, app repo, CI, and run tools/gen_rtm.py and tools/check_sad.py on each change.

Title: Sign in with Google
User story: As a student, I can sign in with my Google account through my browser, so that I do not create a new password.
Functional requirements: FR-AUTH-001; FR-AUTH-002; FR-AUTH-003; FR-AUTH-004; FR-AUTH-005; FR-AUTH-006; FR-AUTH-007; FR-AUTH-008; FR-AUTH-009

Title: Privacy notice, consent and age check
User story: As a student, I see what data is collected and agree before I continue, so that I stay in control of my data.

Title: Create and manage my profile
User story: As a student, I can set my name and optional college details, and only I can see them.
Functional requirements: FR-PROF-002; FR-PROF-003; FR-PROF-004; FR-PROF-005; FR-PROF-006; FR-PROF-007; FR-PROF-008

Title: Request data export or deletion
User story: As a student, I can ask for my data to be exported or deleted, and the action is audited.

Title: Backend foundation (technical enabler)
User story: As the team, we have an API contract, structured logs with correlation IDs, database migrations and generated traceability, so that later work stays consistent.

Title: Browse the lab catalogue
User story: As a student, I can see available labs with difficulty, prerequisites and supported systems.

Title: Download and cache a verified lab bundle
User story: As a student, I can download a lab, trust that it is unmodified, and open it offline.

Title: Keep my attempt on one lab version
User story: As a student, my attempt does not change when a new lab version is published, and I am told a newer one exists.

Title: Author a lab as files with CI checks
User story: As a content author, I write a lab as files and CI proves the starter fails, the reference solution passes and results are repeatable.

Title: Publish, roll back and record content
User story: As an operator, I approve a lab, publish an immutable version, roll back by republishing, and keep a record of who published what.

Title: See whether my computer is ready
User story: As a student, I see which tools are ready, missing or incompatible, and nothing is reinstalled needlessly.
Functional requirements: FR-ENV-001; FR-ENV-002; FR-ENV-003; FR-ENV-009; FR-ENV-012; FR-ENV-013

Title: Approve and run setup safely
User story: As a student, I review a setup plan and consent before anything is installed, and nothing runs with permanent admin rights.

Title: Create the project environment and recover from failure
User story: As a student, my project environment is created from the lab's lockfile, checked afterwards, and failures explain how to recover.

Title: Work on Windows, Linux and macOS
User story: As a student on Windows, Linux or macOS, the core flow works the same way.

Title: Open the lab workspace
User story: As a student, I get a native editor, terminal and my guide side by side, chosen by the lab.

Title: Run lab tasks with limits
User story: As a student, I can run lab tasks that have time and output limits via the local worker, and stop them at any time.
Functional requirements: FR-EXEC-001; FR-EXEC-002; FR-EXEC-003; FR-EXEC-005; FR-EXEC-006; FR-EXEC-009

Title: Stay in control of what runs
User story: As a student, nothing risky or AI-proposed runs without my approval, and I am told which commands are tracked.

Title: Responsive interface
User story: As a student, the interface stays responsive and shows progress during long operations.

Title: Follow a step-by-step guide
User story: As a student, I follow ordered steps with copyable snippets and explanations, and can revisit completed steps.
Functional requirements: FR-GUIDE-001; FR-GUIDE-002; FR-GUIDE-003; FR-GUIDE-004; FR-GUIDE-005; FR-GUIDE-007

Title: Check my own work locally
User story: As a student, I can run practice checks and understanding checks, clearly labelled as unverified.

Title: Save and recover my progress
User story: As a student, my progress is saved after every step and survives a crash.

Title: Sync progress and work offline
User story: As a student, my progress syncs without duplicates, I can work offline, and I can continue on another device.

Title: Ask the tutor with context I control
User story: As a student, I choose what the tutor sees and I give consent before my code is sent to a cloud provider.

Title: Get hints that teach, not only answers
User story: As a student, the tutor explains and gives progressive help up to the lab's limit and never claims code is correct.

Title: AI through a protected proxy with limits
User story: As the team, AI requests pass through our backend that holds the key and enforces per-student limits.

Title: Keep secrets and attacks out of prompts
User story: As a student, secrets are removed before sending, and malicious text in files cannot control the tutor.

Title: Keep working when AI is down
User story: As a student, when AI fails I get a clear message and everything else keeps working.

Title: Submit my work for verification
User story: As a student, I review which files are sent, exclude secrets, and upload a snapshot for grading.

Title: Grade in an isolated sandbox
User story: As the team, student code runs only in a disposable sandbox with no network and no secrets, away from our data.

Title: Compute official scores on the server
User story: As a student, I get a Verified result computed from the grader's signed output, with per-check feedback that does not reveal tests.

Title: Practice results are labelled
User story: As a student, any result computed on my machine is marked Practice and never counted as official.

Title: Reliable and repeatable grading
User story: As a student, resubmitting never doubles my points, grader failures are not held against me, and I see queue status and history.

Title: Grader resists cheating and hostile code
User story: As the team, the grader rejects forged results, off-list dependencies and tampered tests, and passes our hostile-submission suite.

Title: Fair scoring rules
User story: As a student, my setup readiness is shown apart from my score, and using the tutor never lowers my score.

Title: Security review before the pilot
User story: As the team, we complete the threat model, dependency scanning and untrusted-input rules.

Title: Privacy and legal readiness
User story: As the team, retention, legal review and access rules are approved before real students join.

Title: Usability and accessibility
User story: As a beginner, I can find the next action, use the keyboard, and understand every error.
Non-functional requirements: NFR-UX-001; NFR-UX-002; NFR-UX-003; NFR-UX-004; NFR-UX-005; NFR-UX-006; NFR-UX-007

Title: Fast start and detection
User story: As a student, the Flutter desktop app starts and checks my machine within the target times.

Title: Backups, degraded mode and rollback
User story: As the team, backups are restored in a rehearsal, outages show clear messages, and bad content can be reversed.

Title: Cost control
User story: As the team, budgets and alerts exist and we report cost per active student.

Title: Every requirement has a test record
User story: As the team, each MVP requirement has a named test or inspection record.

Title: Browse and filter challenges
User story: As a student, I can find bug-fixing challenges by technology and difficulty and see my attempt history.

Title: Define and validate a challenge
User story: As a content author, I define a bug challenge from a reviewed repository and CI proves it fails first and passes with the fix.

Title: Work on a clean copy of buggy code
User story: As a student, I get a clean copy at a pinned commit, can reset it, and the guide opens the right file.

Title: Investigate with the tutor
User story: As a student, the tutor guides me to reproduce, locate and test, without revealing the fix.

Title: Verified bug-fix grading
User story: As a student, my fix is graded against hidden regression tests and out-of-scope changes are flagged.

Title: Check Git readiness
User story: As a student, I see whether Git, my Git identity and my GitHub access are each ready.

Title: Safe branch and remote checks
User story: As a student, I see repository status and the app checks my branch and remote before I open a PR.

Title: Get my own template repository
User story: As a student, I receive a personal practice repository from an approved template with my own issue variant.

Title: Track my pull request
User story: As a student, the platform links my PR to my attempt and I review my PR description before submitting.

Title: Secure webhooks and CI
User story: As the team, webhooks are verified, duplicate events are ignored, and untrusted PR code never receives secrets.

Title: Points and review
User story: As a student, I earn points from verified PR state, never twice, and maintainers can review or override with a reason.
Functional requirements: FR-OSS-008; FR-OSS-010; FR-OSS-011; FR-OSS-012; FR-OSS-013; FR-OSS-016; FR-OSS-017

Title: Platform hardening and OS parity
User story: As a student on Windows, Linux or macOS, platform hardening and full OS parity are verified.

Title: Run the pilot (10 to 20 students) and fix findings
User story: Acceptance gates in SRS Section 10.1; no new requirements.
